info.title: Dynamic App Service API
info.description:
API for managing dynamic database applications with support for tables, records,
and row-level security.

## Concepts

- **Apps**: Top-level containers. Each app has its own isolated database.
- **Tables**: Structured data storage within an app, defined by a column schema.
- **Records**: Individual rows within a table.
- **Users**: Identities within an app for authentication and access control.
- **Policies**: Row-level security rules on tables that auto-filter queries per user role.

## Resource types (per app)

Currently implemented: **tables**, **files**.
Planned: **workflows**.

patch.description:
Modifies a table's schema in place using ALTER TABLE — the table is not dropped or recreated.
Existing rows are preserved, but `deleteColumns` permanently removes column data and
`updateColumns` type changes may fail if existing data cannot be cast to the new type.

All fields in the request body are optional. An empty body `{}` is a no-op.

**Execution order:** addColumns → updateColumns (type/unique) → updateColumns (rename) → deleteColumns → columnOrder.
All changes run in a single transaction — if any step fails, everything rolls back.

**Constraints:**
- The `id` column cannot be deleted or renamed.
- Type changes use Postgres `ALTER COLUMN ... TYPE ... USING col::new_type`. If the cast is impossible (e.g. text `"abc"` → integer), the entire transaction rolls back.
- `columnOrder` only affects the column order in API responses (metadata), not the physical Postgres column order.
- Adding a UNIQUE constraint (via `updateColumns[].unique = true`) fails with 409 if duplicate values exist.

200.description: Table schema updated — returns the updated Table object

post.description:
Executes a raw SQL query against the application's database.
Use parameterized queries (`$1`, `$2`, ...) to prevent SQL injection.

**Params** can be plain values (passed as text) or typed objects for
date/time/numeric columns that require native Python types:
- Plain: `"params": ["landscapes", 50]`
- Typed: `"params": [{"value": "2024-01-01", "type": "date"}]`
- Mixed: `"params": [{"value": "2024-01-01", "type": "date"}, "landscapes"]`

Supported types: `text`, `integer`, `float`, `boolean`, `date`, `datetime`, `time`
(same as column types). When `type` is omitted, the value is passed as-is.

**Important — quoting identifiers in raw SQL:** The structured API (records, filters,
aggregation) automatically double-quotes all identifiers. Raw SQL queries do NOT —
you must double-quote identifiers yourself in these cases:
- **SQL reserved words** (e.g., `order`, `user`, `value`, `group`):
  `SELECT "order", "value" FROM "my_table" WHERE "user" = $1`
- **camelCase or mixed-case column names** (e.g., `sortOrder`, `createdAt`):
  PostgreSQL lowercases unquoted identifiers, so `sortOrder` becomes `sortorder`
  which won't match. Always quote: `SELECT "sortOrder", "createdAt" FROM deals`
- **Rule of thumb:** when in doubt, double-quote all table and column names in raw SQL.

query.example: SELECT * FROM gallery_items WHERE category = $1 ORDER BY year DESC

params.description:
Bind parameters for the query (prevents SQL injection).
Each element can be either:
- A plain value (string, number, boolean) — passed as-is
- A typed object `{"value": ..., "type": "date"}` — coerced to the
  native Python type asyncpg requires (date, datetime, time, int, float, bool)

readonly.description: If true, only SELECT queries are allowed. Non-admin users are always forced to readonly regardless of this value.

value.query: SELECT * FROM gallery_items WHERE category = $1 ORDER BY year DESC
SELECT side, COUNT(*) as trades FROM trade_data WHERE trade_date >= $1 AND trade_date < $2 GROUP BY side
SELECT * FROM trade_data WHERE side = $1 AND trade_date >= $2
INSERT INTO gallery_items (title, category, year) VALUES ($1, $2, $3)

get.description: Retrieves records with filtering, sorting, joins, field selection, and pagination.

parameters.name: filter
parameters.description:
JSON filter criteria using FilterCondition format (`field`/`op`/`value`).

**Single condition:** `{"field":"year","op":"gt","value":"2020"}`

**AND/OR:** `{"and":[{"field":"year","op":"ge","value":"2020"},{"field":"category","op":"eq","value":"landscapes"}]}`

**Joined-table columns (prefix with table name):** `{"field":"categories.label","op":"eq","value":"Landscapes"}`

**Operators:** eq, ne, lt, gt, le, ge, in, like

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description:
Sort order. Supports multi-column sorting (comma-separated).
Format: `column:direction` where direction is `asc` or `desc` (default: `asc`).

Examples: `year:desc`, `category:asc,year:desc`, `title`

parameters.name: join
parameters.description:
Related tables to join (comma-separated), based on relations defined in the table schema.
Joined data appears as a nested JSON object under the table name key in each record.

Example response with `?join=categories`:
`{"id": 42, "title": "...", "category_id": 1, "categories": {"id": 1, "label": "Landscapes"}}`

parameters.name: fields
parameters.description:
Fields to return (comma-separated, default all).
For joined tables, use table prefix: `id,title,categories.label`

post.description:
Columns marked `autoGenerated` (e.g., the default `id` column) are silently
ignored if included in the request body — the server assigns their values.
Only supply user-defined columns.

post.description:
Execute one or more aggregation functions (count, sum, avg, min, max) with
optional grouping, filtering, having, sorting, and limit.

Supports multiple aggregations in a single request. Each aggregation specifies
a function and an optional field (field is required for sum, avg, min, max but
not for count).

**Result column naming:** Each aggregation result is named `{function}_{field}`
(e.g., `sum_dealValue`, `avg_price`, `max_year`). Count without a field is just `count`.
Column name casing is preserved (camelCase fields stay camelCase in the result key).

post.description:
Creates a row-level security policy on the table. Policies define filter
conditions that are automatically applied to queries based on the
requesting user's identity.

When multiple policies exist for the same operation, they are combined
with OR (permissive) — a row is visible if **any** matching policy allows it.

**Special variables in conditions:**
- `:current_user_id` — replaced with the authenticated user's ID
- `:current_user_roles` — replaced with the user's roles (for `in` operator)

ownerOnly.summary: Users see only their own rows

## Relationship rules

To create a foreign key relationship between two tables, use the `relations` array.
The `referencesColumn` must be either a PRIMARY KEY or a UNIQUE column on the referenced table.
Every table has an auto-generated `id` (SERIAL PRIMARY KEY) unless you define your own.

There are two ways to define the FK column:

**Option A — Implicit FK column (targeting `id`):**
Omit the `foreignKeyColumn` from the `columns` array and the system auto-creates it
as an INTEGER column. Use this when linking to the referenced table's `id` (integer PK).

```json
{
  "name": "posts",
  "columns": [
    {"name": "title", "type": "text"}
  ],
  "relations": [{
    "type": "many-to-one",
    "foreignKeyColumn": "author_id",
    "referencesTable": "authors",
    "referencesColumn": "id"
  }]
}
```
Result: `author_id INTEGER REFERENCES authors(id)` is auto-created.

**Option B — Explicit FK column (targeting a unique column):**
Define the `foreignKeyColumn` in the `columns` array with a matching type, and set `unique: true`
on the target column. Use this when linking to a non-PK unique column (e.g., a text slug).

```json
{
  "name": "categories",
  "columns": [
    {"name": "label", "type": "text"},
    {"name": "slug", "type": "text", "unique": true}
  ]
}
```
```json
{
  "name": "posts",
  "columns": [
    {"name": "title", "type": "text"},
    {"name": "category_slug", "type": "text"}
  ],
  "relations": [{
    "type": "many-to-one",
    "foreignKeyColumn": "category_slug",
    "referencesTable": "categories",
    "referencesColumn": "slug"
  }]
}
```
Result: `FOREIGN KEY (category_slug) REFERENCES categories(slug)`.

**Important:** When bootstrapping multiple tables in a single request (e.g., via POST /apps),
tables must be ordered so that referenced tables appear before the tables that reference them.

name.description: Table name in the database. Must match `[a-z][a-z0-9_]*`, max 63 characters.

description.description: Human-readable description of the table's purpose.
description.example: Items displayed in the image gallery.

columns.description:
Column definitions. If no `id` column is provided, an auto-incrementing
`id` (SERIAL PRIMARY KEY) is added automatically.

Columns referenced by a relation's `foreignKeyColumn` that are NOT listed here
will be auto-created as `INTEGER` columns (suitable for FK to `id`).
If you need a different type (e.g., `text` for a slug FK), you must define
the column explicitly in this array.

relations.description:
Foreign key relations to other tables.
The `referencesColumn` must be a PRIMARY KEY or UNIQUE column on the referenced table.

TablePatch.description:
Partial update to a table's schema. All fields are optional. An empty object `{}` is a no-op.
The table is altered in place — not dropped and recreated.

displayName.description: New display name for the table (metadata only).

description.description: New description for the table (metadata only).

addColumns.description: Columns to add. Each uses the same schema as table creation. New columns default to NULL for existing rows.

deleteColumns.description: Column names to permanently remove (including their data). Cannot delete `id`.

updateColumns.description:
Columns to modify, identified by `name`. Only provided fields are applied — omitted fields
are unchanged. Within each entry: `newName` renames the column, `type` changes the Postgres
type (cast must succeed), `unique` adds/removes a UNIQUE constraint, `displayName` and
`description` update metadata only.

columnOrder.description:
Full list of column names in the desired display order. Must include every column exactly
once, using final names (after any renames). Metadata only — does not change physical
Postgres column order.

ColumnUpdate.description: Identifies an existing column by `name` and applies only the provided changes.

name.description: Current name of the column to modify (lookup key, not changed unless `newName` is set).

newName.description: Rename the column. Cannot rename `id`. The new name must not conflict with existing columns.

type.description:
Change the column's Postgres type. Existing data is cast via `USING col::new_type`.
Fails if any existing value cannot be cast (e.g. text `"abc"` → integer).

unique.description:
`true` adds a UNIQUE constraint (fails with 409 if duplicate values exist).
`false` removes the UNIQUE constraint. Omit to leave unchanged.

name.description: Column name. Must match `[a-zA-Z_][a-zA-Z0-9_]*`, max 63 characters.

displayName.description: Human-readable display name for the column.

description.description: Human-readable description of what this column stores.
description.example: The URL of the category's thumbnail image.

type.description:
Column data type. For date/time types, values are accepted as ISO 8601 strings
and automatically converted:
- `date` — `YYYY-MM-DD` (e.g., `"2025-08-01"`)
- `datetime` — ISO 8601 with optional timezone (e.g., `"2025-08-04T09:49:00"`, `"2025-08-04T09:49:00Z"`, `"2025-08-04T09:49:00+08:00"`)
- `time` — `HH:MM` or `HH:MM:SS` (e.g., `"09:30"`, `"14:30:00"`)

unique.description:
When `true`, a SQL UNIQUE constraint is added to this column.
Unique columns can be used as `referencesColumn` in a Relation (foreign key target).

autoGenerated.description:
Read-only. Present on columns automatically created by the system
(e.g., the default `id` PRIMARY KEY column). Values for these columns
are silently stripped from createRecord requests — do not supply them.

Relation.description:
Defines a foreign key relationship from this table to another table.
Reads naturally as: "foreignKeyColumn `X` references `referencesTable`.`referencesColumn`",
mirroring SQL's `FOREIGN KEY (X) REFERENCES table(column)`.

**Key rules:**
1. `referencesTable` must already exist (or appear earlier in a bootstrap array).
2. `referencesColumn` must be PRIMARY KEY or UNIQUE on the referenced table.
   Every table has `id` (PK) by default; use `"unique": true` on a column to make it eligible.
3. `foreignKeyColumn` is the column on *this* table that holds the foreign key value.
   - If `foreignKeyColumn` is listed in `columns`, a `FOREIGN KEY` constraint is added and the column type must match the target.
   - If `foreignKeyColumn` is NOT listed in `columns`, an `INTEGER` column is auto-created (suitable for referencing integer PKs).

foreignKeyColumn.description:
Column on *this* table that stores the foreign key value.
If not listed in `columns`, an INTEGER column is auto-created.
If listed in `columns`, its type should match the referenced column's type.

referencesTable.description: Name of the table being referenced. Must already exist.

referencesColumn.description:
Column on the referenced table.
Must be PRIMARY KEY (`id`) or have `unique: true`.

userId.description: User ID from the external JWT provider

roles.description: User roles for API authorization and RLS policies. 'admin' is reserved for admin API access.

userId.description: User ID from the external JWT provider

roles.description: Roles to assign. Must include at least one. 'admin' grants admin API access.

aggregations.description: One or more aggregation functions to apply. `field` is required for sum, avg, min, max but not for count.

field.description: Column to aggregate on (not needed for count)

join.description: Related tables to join (based on relations defined in the table schema). Joined columns can be referenced in groupBy, filter, and having with table prefix (e.g., `categories.label`).

groupBy.description: Columns to group results by (prefix with table name for joined columns, e.g., `categories.label`)

filter.description: Filter criteria applied before aggregation (WHERE clause). Same syntax as records filter.

having.description: Filter criteria applied after aggregation (HAVING clause). References aggregate result aliases (e.g., `count`, `avg_price`).

sort.description: Sort order for results, e.g. `count:desc` or `avg_price:asc`

limit.description: Maximum number of grouped results to return

Record.description: A record as flat key-value pairs. Always includes an `id` column (auto-generated if not defined in the table schema). All other columns are as defined by the user.

id.description: Row ID (auto-generated SERIAL if not defined in table schema)

operation.description: Which operations this policy applies to

role.description:
Who this policy applies to:
- `"authenticated"` — any authenticated user
- `"public"` — unauthenticated access
- A role name (e.g., `"editor"`, `"admin"`) — users who have this role

condition.description:
Filter condition auto-applied to queries. Uses the same filter syntax
as the records endpoint. Set to null for unconditional access.

Special variables:
- `:current_user_id` — the requesting user's ID
- `:current_user_roles` — the requesting user's roles

value.description: Comparison value (string, number, boolean, or array for `in`)

TypedParam.description:
A query bind parameter with an explicit type for proper coercion.
Use this for date, datetime, time, integer, float, or boolean columns
where asyncpg requires native Python types instead of plain strings.

value.description: The parameter value as a string or number.

type.description:
The column type to coerce the value to. Uses the same type names
as the Column `type` field.
